suites.label: Core runtime regression
suites.purpose: Did a change to the iii Engine, its workers or the Harness break a core capability agents rely on every day? Nine short, deterministic tasks each exercise one capability: updating saved state, switching to a replaced function, waking on a timer, editing and testing code with the shell and coder workers, database migrations in transactions, parallel agents writing to one table, validators that reject a turn, long sessions that read more than the agent can keep verbatim, and instructions hidden in tool output. Not covered: whole applications, Console pages, browsers, Workers started by Compose and multi-hour work (see Application builds and changes, and Linkly).

suites.label: Application builds and changes
suites.purpose: Can an agent running on iii build and change real software end to end, and does it still work when an independent checker runs it? The suite has a seven-chapter Kanban app (iii functions, Compose, browser); a feature in iii's own Registry, then an independent check of that delivery by a second agent; a website built from a written spec; Alertmanager's Go routing moved into an iii function; and three Workers with their own Console pages (chess, issue form, CI simulator). Not covered: isolated runtime primitives (Core runtime regression) and Registry planning or environment setup, which run only as diagnostics.

suites.label: Build Linkly from the tutorial
suites.purpose: Does the agentic tutorial we point users to still work? One long session builds the Linkly link shortener on a fresh linkly-agentic scaffold, chapter by chapter, adding workers through Compose. It then checks that a request to restart the whole project is refused. Not covered: other templates or tutorials. The seven chapters are one test with one score, so the result does not say which chapter broke unless you open the criteria.

suites.label: Complete the onboarding tour
suites.purpose: Can a new user still finish the onboarding we hand them? One session on a fresh harness project with the tour's worker, as iii project init --learn-iii creates it, sends each tour step's prompt under the harness template's Onboarding profile: say hello, add a database, list what the system can do, build a reactive TODO worker with a Console page, then remove the tour. The test plays the tour page: it closes the button steps, closes each agent step when its trigger fires, and checks the TODO items off as the user would. Not covered: the setup wizard and the tour's on-screen guidance (the page, the spotlight and the panels it opens).

suites.label: Essential checks before merge
suites.purpose: Before merging a change to iii, do the four most basic agent paths still work? The four paths: one exact state write at minimal cost, a safe update of saved data, adapting to a replaced function, and fixing code with the shell and coder workers. Not covered: timers, subagents, databases, validators, long context and prompt injection (all in Core runtime regression), and anything visual.

suites.label: Published stack checks
suites.purpose: Run five checks on the published stack: one precise state write, state persistence, adapting to a changed tool contract, repairing Python code, and timer wake-ups.

suites.label: Application builds and changes ×3 (weekly)
suites.purpose: Once a week, the tests of Application builds and changes run three independent times on the same stack, to measure how much that suite's results vary when nothing changed.

suites.label: Null agent canary
suites.purpose: Proves that no Core runtime regression test gives points or a completion to an agent that does nothing: run with the null-agent profile, which answers done and calls no function, every test must score 0 and stay incomplete, and any point or completion is a hole in that test's evaluator.
